baseline: Short the probes, then check known V022-V016 once to establish actual pad-contact resistance. Prior shorted tips were about 0.5 ohm; use today's reading.
method: Battery and programmer disconnected; use resistance mode.
A stable reading close to the known connected-pair baseline supports a DC connection. Recheck near-zero hits with probes reversed; do not rely on a beep alone.
Record actual ohms, kohms, OL, or a changing reading. Tens/hundreds of ohms, one-way conduction or a changing reading are not direct-copper confirmation.
A very low-resistance path can include a zero-ohm link or an inductor; continuity maps electrical connectivity, not exact buried-layer track geometry.
Only B3 remains in this batch. V064-V075 is confirmed, but V064-V070 is unreported. All seven capacitor comparisons returned OL; broad capacitor-pair testing is retired.

tests.reason: V075 is now confirmed on regulated VDD. This DIFFERENT test checks the older assumption that V070, the free end of R18, is also on that rail. The Q7/R19 photo suggests a possible supply-switch arrangement in which R18 could instead carry a control signal.
tests.confidence: Diagnostic check of an older supply hypothesis, not a predicted hit. Q7 terminal functions and the R18 route remain provisional.
tests.positive_action: Record V070 as regulated VDD after reviewing the resistance; re-evaluate the local Q7/R18 topology before merging device terminals.
tests.negative_action: Withdraw the R18 supply hypothesis if a direct tie is excluded. Trace its local Q7 pad, then choose a remaining GPIO/control endpoint; do not launch another rail sweep.
